title: Policy parser rewrite to validate probabilistic region weighting and graceful model-downgrade rules
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: The current routing policy engine accepts a heterogeneous mix of legacy boolean region selectors, hard-priority tier lists, and ad-hoc fallback model names. This leads to surprising behaviour in production when customers attempt granular behaviours like probabilistic routing across regions, weighted tier splitting, or automated downgrade to a quantized variant if capacity is low. Bugs we've seen: total weight sums not equal to 1, ambiguous precedence between tier routing and region hints, and silent acceptance of invalid fallback chains that reference non-compatible model variants.

Goal: Rework the policy rule parser and schema validator to explicitly support: probabilistic region weights (floating point weights that must sum to 1 with configurable tolerance), first-class tier routing semantics (primary, warm, cold) with explicit throughput constraints, typed fallback model variant compatibility checks (e.g., model family, quantization, sequence-length support), and clear, deterministic precedence rules between selectors. The validator must emit actionable errors and machine-readable hints to surface migration steps for legacy configs.

Non-goals: Replace runtime router or scheduling heuristics in this ticket; we only extend the compile-time validation and produce a compatibility report and migration helper. Runtime enforcement of capacity constraints is out of scope but we will add metadata hooks for the runtime to consume.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New DSL schema accepts probabilistic region blocks: {region: eu-west-1, weight: 0.25} and enforces weights to sum to 1 +- 1e-6 by default; tolerance configurable by policy metadata.
2) Tier routing blocks must include explicit intent: {tier: primary|warm|cold, min_throughput_rps}. Missing min_throughput_rps produces a warning (P2) and hard-fails in strict mode.
3) Fallback chains are validated against a compatibility matrix; incompatible variant chains are rejected with detailed error that includes which property (dtype/quantization/seq_len) failed validation.
4) Legacy boolean region selectors (region: true/false style) are accepted but generate a migration hint and a one-click suggestion to convert to probabilistic weights.
5) Validator produces a normalized, canonical policy representation (deterministic ordering, explicit defaults filled) that the router can consume.
6) Unit and integration tests cover parser, schema validation, and canonicalization with >=95% branch coverage for new code paths.
7) A migration helper script (CLI) exists to transform legacy policy files into the new canonical form and report any manual review items.
technical_notes:
High-level approach: implement a new staged parser that builds a typed AST (policy -> typed-ast) instead of the current permissive JSON->map pipeline. Validation passes: 1) syntax -> 2) structural schema -> 3) semantic validation (weights sum, tier throughput, fallback compatibility) -> 4) canonicalization.

Schema details to add: probabilistic_region: list of objects {region: string, weight: number} with weight >= 0.0; weights with all-zero are invalid. Provide "weight_tolerance" in policy metadata. FallbackVariant type: {model: string, variant: string, constraints: {max_seq: int, supports_kv_cache: bool, quantization: string}}. Compatibility rules defined by small rule engine (match on family prefix, variant compatibility table loaded from model-catalog).

Error model: errors should include path (dsl.location), error_code (string), human_message, and suggested_fixes (list of strings). For the JSON output artifact we will expose errors as an array of strings in the CLI for now (no nested objects in the artifact), but internal code will use structured errors.

Performance: parser/validator must run under 50ms median for typical policy files (<=200 lines). We will microbench parser and canonicalizer.

Implementation tasks: 1) new typed-ast module (policy/typed_ast.rs) or equivalent in our stack, 2) schema definition (policy/schema/*.yaml/jsonschema), 3) validator engine (policy/validator), 4) migration helper CLI (tools/policy-migrate), 5) tests and fixtures, 6) docs for Console to render migration hints.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (in this ticket): implement validator plus a non-destructive migration helper that emits a canonical policy and a list of manual checks. Phase 2: roll out lint-as-warning on write API (silent for 1 week) then fail-on-write in strict mode behind feature flag. Phase 3: encourage customers to opt into strict mode; provide support-runbook with automated conversion for simple cases. Backward-compatibility shim: runtime will accept canonicalized policy but also continue to handle legacy maps for 6 months. After that we will deprecate legacy acceptance and add telemetry to identify remaining legacy users.
test_plan:
Unit tests: parser edge cases (malformed weights, missing keys), schema fuzz tests with randomized weights, negative tests for incompatibility matrix. Integration tests: end-to-end validation using sample customer policies (small subset of redacted real policies), CLI round-trip tests (policy -> migrate -> validator -> same canonical form). Performance tests: benchmark suite to assert median validation <50ms for policies up to 500 lines. Add CI job that runs a subset of fuzz tests nightly.

Monitoring: add metrics: policy_validate_success, policy_validate_errors_total by error_code, validation_latency_ms histogram. Emit telemetry for migrated policies with migration_type tags.
rollout_strategy:
Step 1: land code behind feature flag; run internal dogfood on staging with synthetic heavy policies. Step 2: enable migration hints in Console for all customers (warnings only). Step 3: offer one-click migration for eligible customers; track opt-ins. Step 4: after 4 weeks of warnings and low rollback rate, enable strict validation in write path for new policies behind an admin rollout. Use canary gating: start with 10% of write traffic, ramp to 100% over 7 days.

Fallback: provide emergency toggle to disable strict validation if regressions occur. Rollback plan documented in playbook with rollback commands and telemetry keys to check.
